overview.heading: How the LinkedIn Banner Maker works
paragraphs: Enter your name or brand and, if you like, a one-line headline. Choose one of ten looks and a color direction, and PiCraft designs a very wide banner at LinkedIn's recommended 1584×396 px, with your text placed in the right half.

The text sits on the right because LinkedIn draws your profile photo over the lower-left of the banner, and it crops the banner a little differently on mobile. The left third is kept calm and free of important details for the same reason.
You download the banner as a JPG, plus a 3168×792 px version at twice the size for sharp display on high-resolution screens.

whatYouGet.title: 1584×396 px banner
whatYouGet.description: A JPG at LinkedIn's recommended cover image size and 4:1 ratio, well under the file size limit.

whatYouGet.title: A 2× high-resolution copy
whatYouGet.description: A 3168×792 px JPG for crisp results on large and high-density screens.

whatYouGet.title: Text placed to survive cropping
whatYouGet.description: Your name and headline sit in the right half, away from the profile photo and the mobile crop.

whatYouGet.title: Ten looks
whatYouGet.description: Gradients, skylines, nature, workspaces, geometric shapes and more, to fit your industry.

whatYouGet.title: Your colors
whatYouGet.description: Add a color direction such as "navy and teal" to match your brand or your profile photo.

useCases.title: Job seekers
useCases.description: A clean banner with your name and a short headline makes a profile look finished and intentional.

useCases.title: Freelancers and consultants
useCases.description: Use the headline to state what you do and who you do it for, so visitors understand your offer at a glance.

useCases.title: Founders and small businesses
useCases.description: Reflect your brand colors on a founder profile that people see after meeting you or reading your posts.

useCases.title: Creators and speakers
useCases.description: Show your name and topic with a style that matches your content, whether calm, premium or energetic.

useCases.title: Recruiters and sales teams
useCases.description: Give a team a consistent look by using the same style and colors for every profile.

tips.title: Say what you do, not just who you are
tips.description: "Product designer · Helping fintech teams ship faster" tells a visitor more than a job title alone.

tips.title: Keep the headline short
tips.description: Under 60 characters keeps the text large enough to read on mobile.

tips.title: Match your profile photo
tips.description: Pick colors that work with your photo's background and clothing, so the banner and portrait look like a set.

tips.title: Choose calm over busy
tips.description: Text over a busy image is hard to read. Soft gradients, bokeh and solid blocks give the cleanest result.

tips.title: Preview on desktop and mobile
tips.description: After uploading, check your profile on both. The banner is cropped differently on each.

tips.title: Use your own brand colors
tips.description: Name two colors in the colors field, such as "deep green and cream", to keep the banner consistent with your website.

tips.title: Refresh it occasionally
tips.description: Update the headline when your role or focus changes so the banner stays accurate.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a banner look
styleGuide.intro: The look sets the background. Pick the one that fits your industry and the impression you want to leave.

items.title: Soft gradient
items.description: A smooth blend of two colors. Works for nearly every profession.

items.title: Abstract tech
items.description: Flowing lines and digital patterns. Fits software, data and product roles.

items.title: City skyline
items.description: Urban silhouettes. Fits real estate, finance, law and consulting.

items.title: Calm nature
items.description: Soft landscapes. Fits coaching, wellness, sustainability and education.

items.title: Desk & workspace
items.description: A tidy desk scene. Fits designers, writers and freelancers.

items.title: Geometric shapes
items.description: Clean shapes and angles. Fits architects, engineers and designers.

items.title: Ocean & waves
items.description: Open water and movement. Fits travel, hospitality and leadership profiles.

items.title: Dark & premium
items.description: Deep tones with subtle highlights. Fits luxury, strategy and executive profiles.

items.title: Soft bokeh lights
items.description: Blurred light points. Fits event, media and creative roles.

items.title: Solid color block
items.description: A flat color with the text on top. The most readable option and the easiest to match to a brand.

checklist.heading: Before you upload to LinkedIn
items: Check that your name is spelled correctly. It is the one word that must be right.
Upload the 1584×396 px file first, and use the 3168×792 px version if the banner looks soft on large screens.
Open your profile on a phone and on a computer to confirm that the text is not covered by your photo.
Make sure the headline matches the headline and About section of your profile, so your story is consistent.
Keep the file under 8 MB. The files PiCraft exports are well below that.
Use JPG or PNG. LinkedIn's help page lists these as the supported types.
Reposition the banner in LinkedIn's editor if your text sits too close to an edge.

limits: The banner is designed for personal profiles. LinkedIn company pages use a different cover size, which the [LinkedIn banner size guide](/sizes/linkedin-banner-size) compares with the personal one.
Your profile photo covers part of the lower-left, and mobile crops the sides, so the maker cannot keep every pixel visible on every device.
The text is part of the image. To change a word, generate again.
The maker does not add logos or photos of you. Upload those in LinkedIn or an editor afterwards.
The name field is required, so every banner has a focal text. A short slogan can take the place of a name.
